title: Theft protection
summary: Sua conta → Proteção contra roubo (ADR 0044, ADR 0045, ADR 0051, security.md rule 14, bipe-chat/bipe#600, bipe-chat/bipe#125). First the row Proteção do celular: the phone's own theft protection (ADR 0045 tier 0). The owner picks 1 to 3 guardians from verified contacts. A guardian sees the accounts they protect and can mark one as stolen, or clear the mark.

name.description: The display name the app knows, else the @ (POST /v1/handles/resolve), else the Matrix ID.

userId.description: The Matrix ID of an account that chose the user.

markedAt.description: Set while a mark is on (GuardedAccount.mark.stolen_at).

osPath.description: The path text for this phone in the row Proteção do celular, above the guardians, always shown. iOS: bipe_os_theft_path_ios_face_id, or bipe_os_theft_path_ios_touch_id when LAContext.biometryType is touchID. Android: bipe_os_theft_path_samsung when Build.MANUFACTURER is samsung, else bipe_os_theft_path_android.

guardians.description: At most maxGuardians (registries/theft-protection.json), in the order the server returns.

guarding.description: Accounts that chose the user. Empty: bipe_theft_guarding_empty.

lastMark.description: bipe_theft_last_mark (guardian name, date) when GuardianState.last_mark is set.

of.description: A verified contact that is not a guardian yet.

picker.description: Set while the picker sheet is open. Empty: bipe_theft_picker_empty.

openOsSettings.effect: The row button bipe_os_theft_action opens the phone's settings. iOS: UIApplication.openSettingsURLString. Android: Settings.ACTION_SECURITY_SETTINGS on Samsung, else Settings.ACTION_SETTINGS; Settings.ACTION_SETTINGS when the first intent has no activity. Same as onboarding.json target osTheftSettings.

appear.effect: Reads GET /v1/me/guardians and sets guardians, guarding and lastMark. Runs again when the app comes to the foreground.

openPicker.effect: Lists verified contacts (UserIdentity.isVerified, the in-person check of rule 3) that are not guardians. Disabled with bipe_theft_guardians_full at maxGuardians.

addGuardian.effect: Asks for the current Bipe PIN (bipe_pin_enter_title), then PUT /v1/me/guardians with the list plus userId and the PIN (bipe-chat/bipe#908). A wrong PIN shows on the PIN pad (bipe_pin_wrong, bipe_pin_blocked_body). Closes the picker.

removeGuardian.effect: Asks for the current Bipe PIN, then PUT /v1/me/guardians without userId and with the PIN (bipe-chat/bipe#908).

userId.description: A protected account without a mark.

askMark.effect: confirm mark: bipe_theft_mark_confirm_title and bipe_theft_mark_confirm_body with the name.

mark.effect: After the owner check of the device (biometric or device PIN): POST /v1/theft/{userId}/mark, then appear.

userId.description: A protected account with a mark.

clear.effect: After the owner check: POST /v1/theft/{userId}/clear, then appear.

notes: Proteção do celular (bipe-chat/bipe#125, ADR 0045 tier 0): the row shows on every visit, also after the Você prompt osTheftProtection was dismissed. It never shows a state. Research of 29 October 2026 (Apple and Google public docs): iOS has no public API that reads Stolen Device Protection, and no public URL that opens Face ID e Código; App-prefs: URLs are private API. Android has no public API that reads Theft Detection Lock or Offline Device Lock, and no public intent for the Theft protection page (it is part of Google Play services). So the app never says the protection is on (security.md rule 14).

OS names, pt-BR (29 October 2026). iOS 17.3 and later: Ajustes > Face ID e Código (Touch ID e Código) > Proteção de Dispositivo Roubado. Stock Android 10 and later, Motorola and Xiaomi HyperOS: Configurações > Google > Todos os serviços > Proteção contra roubo, with Bloqueio de Detecção de Roubo, Bloqueio de Dispositivo Offline and Bloqueio Remoto (Google Brasil). Samsung One UI 7 and later: Configurações > Segurança e privacidade > Proteção do aparelho perdido > Proteção contra roubo. Nobody checked the Motorola and HyperOS names on a device; Google says the path can change a little per maker.
One guardian is enough to mark (ADR 0044 working default). The mark locks the account on the server and ends every session; the stolen phone cannot clear it.
Clearing by CPF with the 72-hour wait (ADR 0051) is not in this version (MZ decision on bipe-chat/bipe#538): a guardian clears, or support after a CPF check by hand.

Every account on the phone sends the phone ID once per start (PUT /v1/me/phone, a random value kept on the phone, never from hardware). A mark then covers the personal accounts on that phone and ends that phone's sessions of a company account (bipe-chat/bipe#268).
The owner sees who set the last mark (lastMark). The mark is account metadata: messages and E2EE do not change.
Never show a Matrix ID where a name or an @ is known.
